title: Reduce the attack surface
briefing: You flagged netcat-traditional. Sign-off says: remove it. Nothing on app-01
needs it, and leaving a ready-made backdoor tool installed is asking for
tips: `apt remove PKG` uninstalls a package (with sudo).
Confirm afterwards with `dpkg -l netcat-traditional` — it should no longer be 'ii'.
objective: Uninstall the netcat-traditional package from app-01.
hints: Remove it as root: `sudo apt remove netcat-traditional`.
`sudo apt remove netcat-traditional` (or `sudo apt purge netcat-traditional` to drop its config too).
After removal, `dpkg -s netcat-traditional` reports it is not installed.
explanation: Removing software you don't need is one of the cheapest security wins there is: every package that isn't installed is one an attacker can't abuse. `apt remove` uninstalls the program; `apt purge` also deletes its config files.
